newsitem.title: USA: Centennial to sell back Century shares.
newsitem.headline: Centennial to sell back Century shares.

text.p: Centennial Technologies Inc said on Friday it agreed to sell 3.93 million shares that it owns in its majority-held subsidiary, Century Electronics Manufacturing Inc to Century.
Centennial said the transaction will reduce its stake in Century to about 45 percent, from 67 percent.
Century will pay for the shares with $1.25 million in cash, a convertible debenture valued at $6.0 million and will repay $4.2 million in intercompany loans to Centennial, it said.
As part of an agreement, Centennial said it will also transfer its majority stake in its Thailand unit to Century.
Century, a contract electronics manufacturer, would retire 3.0 million of the 3.92 million shares Centennial will sell under the agreement, it said.
Centennial said the deal is subject to a number of material conditions. The conditions were not disclosed.
It said the parties plan to close the transaction by the end of June.
Earlier today, DDL Electronics Inc, of Newbury Park, Calif., said it had agreed to acquire Century for 33 million DDL shares.
